title: Custom mechanical keyboards
subtitle: Mechanical keyboards designed and built in 3D-printed and acrylic cases
role: Design, drawings for making, and the builds
summary: In 2023 in Shanghai, I designed and built mechanical keyboards as a personal project. Drawn to how keyboards are structured and put together, I spent time researching their construction, produced every design drawing and processing drawing myself, and tested 3D printing alongside laser-cut acrylic across finished builds.

sections.heading: Drawings before parts
sections.body: The project began from curiosity about how a mechanical keyboard is built and put together. I spent a long time researching before I made anything, and I completed all of the design drawings and processing drawings on my own.

sections.heading: Printing and cutting cases
sections.body: I wanted to feel how different fabrication methods change the same kind of object. One path used 3D printing, moving from a bare white printed frame to a finished board fitted with white keycaps and blue under-glow. The second path used laser-cut acrylic sheets cut over MDF, producing a clear acrylic case with black keycaps and a green acrylic case tested with both mint-green and dark green keycaps.

sections.heading: Bench assembly and details
sections.body: Everything was assembled on the desk, from seating switches part-way onto a PCB through to completed boards in different finishes, including a beige and yellow build, a black board paired with a wrist rest, and a back plate marked REYN DESIGN. No CAD files survive from these builds; the desk photographs remain as the record of what was made.
